comments.content: The binary detection logic has a gap: jschardet may confidently detect an encoding for genuinely binary files (e.g. it often returns 'windows-1252' or similar with non-null encoding), so the `isBinaryFile` check is only reached when detection fails entirely. Consider running `isBinaryFile` first (or in addition) to preserve the previous binary-file guard, otherwise binary files will now be decoded and returned as garbled text instead of throwing.

jschardet's detection includes a confidence score. Relying on any non-null `encoding` regardless of confidence can misclassify short files. Consider gating on a minimum confidence threshold (e.g. `detected.confidence >= 0.5`) before trusting the detected encoding, and falling back to utf8/binary check otherwise.

iconv-lite normalizes encoding names but jschardet can return values like 'ascii', 'ISO-8859-1', etc. The comparison `this.fileEncoding.toLowerCase() !== "utf8"` will treat 'UTF-8' (with hyphen) as non-utf8 and re-encode unnecessarily. Normalize the detected encoding (e.g. strip hyphens / compare against both 'utf-8' and 'utf8', or use `iconv.encodingExists`) to avoid needless re-encoding and potential corruption for ASCII/UTF-8 files.

If jschardet returns an encoding that iconv-lite doesn't support, `iconv.decode` will throw and break file opening. Consider guarding with `iconv.encodingExists(this.fileEncoding)` and falling back to 'utf8' when unsupported.
